$comment: Generated by build-ground-truth.mjs from the running application. Do not edit by hand.

accounts.note: Books and tracks shipments, resolves exceptions.
Receives, puts away, picks and packs.
Invoices, credit notes, claim settlement. Has two-factor on.

shapeMeaning.linked: Server-rendered, reached by an <a href>. A link-following crawler finds these.
shapeMeaning.routed: Client-side routed. The nav control is a <button> calling history.pushState; the body comes from /api/view. A deep link works, but no anchor points here.
shapeMeaning.enclosed: Modals, drawers and tab panels. Real content with no URL of its own, reachable only by clicking.

defects.howToClear: POST /__faults with every id set to false. POST /__faults/reset restores them.
defects.provenance: Written from a freight-software failure taxonomy before any QA NXT generator was read, and not adjusted afterwards.

list.title: A stock adjustment accepts a quantity that drives on-hand below zero
list.detail: The form declares min="1" but the handler applies the delta without checking the resulting balance, so an adjustment of -5000 against 12 on hand stores -4988.
list.observable: Submit an adjustment larger than the on-hand quantity; the stock row then shows a negative on-hand figure.

list.title: A requested delivery date before the collection date is accepted
list.detail: The booking wizard validates each date in isolation. No rule compares them, so a delivery date in the past relative to collection is stored and shown on the shipment.
list.observable: Book a shipment with collection 2026-04-10 and delivery 2026-04-02; it saves.

list.title: The weight unit selector is recorded but never applied
list.detail: A weight entered in pounds is stored as kilograms. The rate is then calculated from a number 2.2 times too small, and the vehicle capacity check passes a load it should refuse.
list.observable: Book with weight 1000 and unit "lb"; the shipment detail shows 1000 kg.

list.title: Two invoices can carry the same reference
list.detail: The reference is generated from a counter held in memory and never checked for uniqueness before insert.
list.observable: Create two invoices quickly; both can be issued with the same INV-2026-xxxx reference.

list.title: The credit limit is checked on the form but not in the handler
list.detail: The browser disables submit when the customer is over limit. The POST handler has no equivalent check, so an order placed against a customer on credit hold is accepted.
list.observable: POST a sales order for a customer whose status is onHold; it is created.

list.title: The fuel surcharge is applied to the VAT-inclusive total
list.detail: The surcharge line is computed as gross x 11.5% instead of net x 11.5%, overcharging every invoice by 2.3% of net.
list.observable: On any invoice, the fuel line does not equal 11.5% of the freight line.

list.title: A weight exactly on a rate band boundary falls into the cheaper band
list.detail: Band selection uses weight < toKg rather than <=, so 50.00 kg is rated in the 0-50 band and 250.00 kg in the 50-250 band. The published card says the boundary belongs to the upper band.
list.observable: Quote 50 kg and 50.01 kg; the rate per kg is the same when the card says it should step.

list.title: Duty on a CIF shipment is calculated without the freight cost
list.detail: Customs value for CIF should include cost, insurance and freight. The declaration uses the goods value alone, understating duty on every CIF consignment.
list.observable: A CIF declaration shows dutyGbp = declaredValue x rate, with no freight component.

list.title: A credit note can be raised for more than the invoice it credits
list.detail: No comparison against the invoice total. A credit note of GBP 50,000 against a GBP 400 invoice is accepted and applied.
list.observable: Raise a credit note above the invoice total; it saves and the customer balance goes negative.

list.title: The result count is taken before the filter is applied
list.detail: The "N shipments" heading and the page count come from the unfiltered collection, so a filter that matches three rows still offers four pages of results.
list.observable: Filter by status=exception; the heading still reports the full count.

list.title: Claim settlement is hidden from a viewer but not refused
list.detail: The settle control is omitted from the page for a role without claim:settle. The POST handler checks only that a session exists, so the same request from a viewer succeeds.
list.observable: Sign in as readonly and POST to the settle endpoint; the claim is settled.

list.title: Any signed-in user can read any shipment by its identifier
list.detail: The detail handler loads by id without checking the shipment belongs to a customer the user is allowed to see. Customer-scoped users can read every other customer's consignments, destinations and declared values.
list.observable: Request a shipment belonging to a different customer; it renders in full.

list.title: A legacy API key holds every scope and has no expiry
list.detail: The "Legacy ETL" key carries all 33 permissions including admin:users, was last used 240 days ago, and the screen offers no way to scope or expire it.
list.observable: The API keys screen lists a key whose scope column reads "all" with no expiry date.

list.title: Cancelling a shipment leaves its route stop active
list.detail: The shipment moves to cancelled. The stop on the planned route keeps its status and sequence, so the driver is still dispatched to collect a consignment that no longer exists.
list.observable: Cancel a shipment that appears on a route; the route detail still lists the stop as pending.

list.title: Going back from step 3 of the booking wizard empties step 2
list.detail: Step 2 is re-rendered from defaults rather than from the draft, so dimensions and special handling are silently cleared when the user steps back.
list.observable: Complete steps 1-3, press Back twice; step 2 fields are blank.

list.title: Submitting the booking form twice creates two shipments
list.detail: No idempotency key and no control disabling. A double click, or a retry after a slow response, produces two consignments and two freight charges.
list.observable: POST the final wizard step twice with the same draft; two shipment references are returned.

list.title: A rejected declaration can be released
list.detail: The release handler does not check the current status, so a declaration customs has rejected can be moved straight to released and the shipment allowed to travel.
list.observable: Release a declaration whose status is rejected; it becomes released.

list.title: A search term over 500 characters returns HTTP 500 with a stack trace
list.detail: The query is compiled into a regular expression without bounding its length, and the failure is rendered with the Node stack.
list.observable: GET /shipments?q=<501 characters>; the response is 500 and contains file paths.

list.title: An oversize evidence upload crashes instead of being refused
list.detail: The form declares a 5 MB limit in its hint. The handler reads the whole body first and throws, so the user sees a 500 rather than a validation message.
list.observable: Upload a file above the stated limit; the response is 500, not a field error.

list.title: An invoice whose shipment has been removed crashes its detail page
list.detail: The detail view dereferences shipment.reference without a guard.
list.observable: Open an invoice whose shipmentId no longer resolves; the response is 500.

list.title: The adjustment quantity input has no label
list.detail: The control carries a placeholder only. A screen reader announces "edit text, blank", and the field is the one that changes stock.
list.observable: The input has no label element, no aria-label and no aria-labelledby.

list.title: Claim form errors are not associated with their fields
list.detail: Validation messages render as plain text above the form with no aria-describedby and no role="alert", so they are neither announced nor reachable from the field.
list.observable: Submit the claim form empty; the messages appear with no programmatic link to the inputs.

list.title: Vehicle availability is conveyed by colour alone
list.detail: The status column renders a coloured square with no text and no accessible name. Available, in maintenance and off road are indistinguishable without colour vision.
list.observable: The status cell contains a styled span with no text content.

list.title: The approval modal is not announced and does not trap focus
list.detail: The dialog has no aria-modal, focus stays on the trigger behind it, and Tab walks the page underneath.
list.observable: Open the approve modal; focus remains on the button that opened it.

list.title: The rate card table forces horizontal scrolling on a phone
list.detail: The table is given a fixed 980px minimum width and is not wrapped in a scroll container, so the whole page scrolls sideways below about 1000px.
list.observable: At 390px wide, document.scrollWidth exceeds the viewport width.

list.title: The route planner is fixed at 1100px
list.detail: The planner grid uses an absolute width rather than a responsive one, so on a tablet the stop list is cut off with no way to reach it.
list.observable: At 768px wide, the planner extends beyond the viewport.

list.title: The audit log takes over three seconds to respond
list.detail: Every entry is enriched by scanning the user list for each row rather than by one lookup, and the whole 120-row set is formatted before the page is cut to 25.
list.observable: GET /admin/audit takes more than 3000 ms.

list.title: The search term is written into the results page unescaped
list.detail: The "no results for X" message interpolates the raw query into the HTML, so a crafted term executes in the operator's session.
list.observable: GET /shipments?q=<script>alert(1)</script> renders the tag rather than its text.

list.title: The stock adjustment form carries no anti-forgery token
list.detail: Every other write form in the application posts a token. This one does not, and the handler accepts a cross-origin form post that changes inventory.
list.observable: The form has no hidden token field and the handler does not require one.

list.title: The "remember me" path reissues the session cookie without HttpOnly
list.detail: The ordinary sign-in sets HttpOnly. The remember-me branch builds the header by hand and omits it, exposing the session token to any script on the page.
list.observable: Sign in with remember me ticked; the Set-Cookie header lacks HttpOnly.

list.title: API errors return the Node stack trace and absolute file paths
list.detail: The JSON error handler serialises the whole error object, disclosing the deployment directory layout and dependency versions.
list.observable: An API error body contains "at " frames and /home/ paths.

list.title: Customer contact email is passed in the query string
list.detail: The contact search submits by GET, so email addresses land in access logs, proxy logs and the browser history of a shared operations terminal.
list.observable: Searching contacts produces /customers?contactEmail=someone@example.test in the address bar.

list.name: Order to cash
list.description: A sales order becomes a shipment, the shipment is planned onto a route and dispatched, the delivery is invoiced and the invoice is paid.
list.breaksAt: the fuel surcharge is 11.5% of net, not of the gross

list.name: Procure to dispatch
list.description: A purchase order is received into stock, put away, picked and packed, with over-receipt refused.

list.name: Carrier onboarding to first booking
list.description: A carrier is added, its rate card is created, onboarding is completed and it becomes bookable.
list.breaksAt: a weight on a band boundary is rated in the upper band

list.name: Exception to claim settlement
list.description: A delivery exception becomes a claim, evidence is attached, a viewer is refused and finance settles it with an audit entry.
list.breaksAt: an oversize upload is refused rather than crashing

list.name: Customs hold to release
list.description: A held declaration gets its missing document, a rejected one is refused release, and the held one is released so its shipment moves on.
list.breaksAt: duty on delivered terms includes the freight cost

list.name: User onboarding to audit trail
list.description: A user is invited into the least-access role, refused a write action, moved to another role with a reason, and the change is audited.
list.breaksAt: the audit log answers quickly enough to be usable
